prompt: For a Wisconsin driver with no prior OWI offenses, what alcohol concentration is the prohibited (per se) limit?
explanation: Wisconsin's prohibited alcohol concentration is 0.08 or more for drivers with two or fewer prior OWI-related offenses.

prompt: A Wisconsin driver has three prior OWI convictions. At what alcohol concentration is this driver over the legal limit?
explanation: With 3 or more prior OWI convictions, suspensions or revocations (or an ignition interlock order), the prohibited alcohol concentration is more than 0.02, not 0.08.

prompt: What is the legal alcohol concentration allowed for Wisconsin drivers under age 21?
explanation: Wisconsin requires absolute sobriety for drivers under 21: the allowed alcohol concentration is 0.00%, so any alcohol in the system is a violation. 0.02% is the rule in many other states, not Wisconsin.

prompt: A 20-year-old Wisconsin driver is stopped after having one beer and tests at 0.01. Which statement is true?
choices: It is legal because it is under 0.08
It is only a violation if the driver is also speeding
It is a violation, because drivers under 21 may not have any alcohol in their system
It is legal because it is under 0.02
explanation: Wisconsin's limit for drivers under 21 is 0.00%, meaning no alcohol at all while driving.

prompt: A 24-year-old learning to drive with a Wisconsin instruction permit has a glass of wine before a practice drive. Why is this illegal even though the driver is over 21?
choices: Permit holders must maintain absolute sobriety no matter their age
It is legal as long as the supervising driver is sober
explanation: WisDOT requires instruction permit holders to maintain absolute sobriety: no alcohol in the system at any time, no matter what their age.

prompt: What is the alcohol concentration limit for a person driving a commercial motor vehicle in Wisconsin?
explanation: Wisconsin law prohibits driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more, half the 0.08 limit for ordinary vehicles.

prompt: Under Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law, what happens if you refuse a police officer's request to take a test for alcohol concentration?
choices: Your license is suspended for 30 days
Nothing, as long as you pass a field sobriety test
You get a warning and can drive home
You are arrested and lose your driving privileges for at least one year
explanation: If you refuse, the officer must arrest you for violating the Implied Consent Law, and you lose your driving privileges for at least one year.

prompt: For a first OWI conviction in Wisconsin, how long does the court revoke the driver's operating privilege?
explanation: A first OWI conviction brings a revocation of not less than 6 months nor more than 9 months; the driver may apply for an occupational license at any time.

prompt: What is the base penalty for a first-offense OWI in Wisconsin (with no prior offenses counted)?
explanation: A first OWI in Wisconsin is a civil forfeiture of $150 to $300 (plus surcharges and costs), not a crime with jail time; later offenses carry fines and jail.

prompt: A driver puts a partly finished bottle of wine in the glove compartment for the ride home. Is this legal in Wisconsin?
choices: Yes, as long as the driver is sober
Yes, because the glove compartment is closed
Yes, if the cork is pushed back in
No, because the glove compartment counts as part of the passenger area
explanation: Wisconsin law treats a utility or glove compartment as within the area normally occupied by the driver and passengers, so an opened container there is illegal. Put it in the trunk.

prompt: What is the minimum age to get a Class D instruction permit in Wisconsin?
explanation: You must be at least 15 years old, pass the knowledge test, signs test and vision screening, and be enrolled in driver education.

prompt: How long must a Wisconsin driver under 18 hold an instruction permit before getting a probationary license?
explanation: Teens must hold the instruction permit at least six months and be at least 16 years old.

prompt: An adult age 18 or older gets a Wisconsin instruction permit. How long must they hold it before getting a probationary license?
explanation: WisDOT says permit holders 18 or older must hold the permit at least seven days; the six-month rule applies to those under 18.

prompt: How many hours of supervised driving must a Wisconsin teen complete before getting a probationary license?
explanation: Teens must log at least 50 hours of practice: 40 during daylight and 10 during darkness. The sponsor verifies the hours.

prompt: Who may supervise a Wisconsin Class D instruction permit holder?
choices: Any licensed driver age 18 or older
A licensed driver with at least two years of driving experience and a valid regular (not probationary) license
explanation: The accompanying driver needs at least two years of licensed driving experience and a valid regular license (not probationary or occupational), and must sit in the front passenger seat.

prompt: A Wisconsin instruction permit holder wants to practice driving after dark. Who must be in the seat beside them?
choices: Any parent, even without a license
Any licensed driver age 19 or older
A qualified instructor or a licensed person at least 25 with two years of driving experience
explanation: During hours of darkness the permit holder must be accompanied by a qualified instructor or a licensed person 25 or older with at least two years of licensed driving experience.

prompt: How long is a Wisconsin Class D instruction permit valid?
explanation: A Class D instruction permit is valid for 18 months and can be renewed. (Motorcycle permits are valid for 6 months.)

prompt: What is the minimum age for a probationary driver license in Wisconsin?
explanation: The first license after the road test is a probationary license, and you must be at least 16 years old.

prompt: How long do Wisconsin's graduated driver license (GDL) passenger and hour restrictions last for a new driver under 18?
explanation: The GDL restrictions apply for the first nine months of the probationary license, unless the driver turns 18 sooner.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a Wisconsin probationary license is convicted of speeding during the GDL period. What happens to the restrictions?
explanation: GDL restrictions are extended six months if the teen is convicted of a moving violation, violates a restriction, or has the license suspended or revoked.

prompt: During the GDL period, a 16-year-old Wisconsin driver wants to drive alone at 1 a.m. When is this allowed?
choices: Only with a sibling in the car
Only when driving between home, school and/or work
explanation: From midnight to 5 a.m., a GDL driver may drive alone only between home, school and/or work; otherwise a parent/guardian or qualified licensed adult must be in the front seat.
ref: Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook, p. 11; Wis. Stat. § 343.085(2m)(a)2.

prompt: During the first nine months of a Wisconsin probationary license (driver under 18), who may ride along?
choices: Any number of immediate family members, one qualified licensed adult, and one other person
explanation: A GDL driver may carry any number of immediate family members, one qualified licensed adult (instructor or spouse 19+, or a person 21+ with two years experience), and only one other person.

prompt: When do Wisconsin's GDL hour and passenger restrictions stop applying, even if nine months have not passed?
choices: Once the driver finishes high school
explanation: Once you turn 18, the graduated driver license hours and passenger restrictions no longer apply.

prompt: What does an adult sponsor accept by signing a Wisconsin teen's driver license application?
choices: Nothing; it is only a formality
A promise to ride along on every trip
Responsibility to pay the teen's insurance premium only
Legal and financial responsibility for incidents caused by the minor's driving
explanation: The sponsor accepts liability, meaning they are legally and financially responsible for incidents caused by the minor driving, and can remove the sponsorship at any time.

prompt: How many demerit points within a 12-month period will get a Wisconsin driver's privilege suspended?
explanation: Accumulating 12 or more demerit points within any 12-month period leads to suspension or revocation.

prompt: A Wisconsin probationary license holder gets a second traffic conviction. How are the demerit points for that conviction handled?
explanation: If you hold a probationary license, an instruction permit, or no license, demerit points are doubled on the second and later convictions (vehicle equipment violations excepted).

prompt: Who is a habitual traffic offender in Wisconsin?
choices: Someone convicted of 4 or more major or 12 or more minor violations within five years
Anyone who refuses a breath test
Anyone with 2 speeding tickets in a year
explanation: A habitual offender has four or more major traffic violations or 12 or more minor violations within five years.

prompt: How long is a Wisconsin habitual traffic offender's driving privilege revoked?
explanation: Habitual traffic offenders lose their driving privilege for five years, though they may qualify for an occupational license after a two-year wait.

prompt: What is Wisconsin's minimum liability insurance coverage for injury or death of one person?
explanation: Wisconsin minimums are $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for more than one person, and $10,000 for property damage.

prompt: What minimum liability coverage does Wisconsin require for property damage?
explanation: Wisconsin requires at least $10,000 of property damage liability coverage (along with $25,000/$50,000 for bodily injury).

prompt: How many questions are on Wisconsin's Class D knowledge test, and how many must you answer correctly?
explanation: The knowledge test has 50 questions and you must answer 40 (80%) correctly. The highway signs test is a separate test.

prompt: How many questions are on Wisconsin's separate highway signs test, and how many must be correct to pass?
explanation: The highway signs test has 15 questions and you must answer 12 (80%) correctly.

prompt: What visual acuity does Wisconsin require for a regular car license applicant?
choices: At least 20/40 in one eye (corrected or uncorrected)
explanation: Wisconsin requires visual acuity of at least 20/40 in one eye, corrected or uncorrected, and a 70-degree field of vision from the center of each eye.

prompt: You move to Wisconsin with a valid regular driver license from another state. Within how many days should you apply for a Wisconsin license?
explanation: New residents with a regular out-of-state license should apply within 60 days after moving. CDL holders should apply within 30 days.

prompt: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle in Wisconsin?
choices: The driver and all passengers, at any age
explanation: Wisconsin law requires you and your passengers to wear seat belts at any age, even in vehicles with air bags.

prompt: According to the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook, until about what ages do children generally ride in a child safety seat and then a booster seat?
explanation: Generally, children must be in a child safety seat until they reach age four and in a booster seat until age eight.

prompt: Under Wisconsin law, a child must ride in a rear-facing child seat until reaching at least what?
explanation: A child who is less than one year old or weighs less than 20 pounds must be in a rear-facing seat, in a back seat if the vehicle has one.

prompt: Which Wisconsin drivers may not send or compose a text message while driving?
explanation: Wisconsin bans all drivers from composing or sending text or email messages while driving; voice-operated or hands-free use is exempt.

prompt: A 17-year-old with a Wisconsin probationary license wants to take a hands-free call while driving. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, if a parent is calling
Yes, if the call is under one minute
Yes, hands-free calls are always allowed
No, permit and probationary license holders may use a phone only to report an emergency
explanation: Instruction permit and probationary license holders can only use a cell phone to report an emergency; the ban includes hands-free use.

prompt: When may a Wisconsin driver use a hand-held cell phone while driving through a highway construction zone?
choices: Only when no workers are visible
Any time traffic is moving slowly
Only to use a GPS app
explanation: You can only use your cellphone in a construction zone if you are reporting an emergency; hands-free, voice-operated use is the only other exception.

prompt: What does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook say about headphones while driving?
choices: Do not drive with headsets or headphones that cover or go in both ears
Headphones are fine at low volume
Headphones are required on the freeway
explanation: Do not drive with headsets or headphones that cover or go in both ears, and keep the radio low enough to hear emergency vehicles.

prompt: What following distance does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook teach in good conditions?
explanation: Wisconsin teaches the Four Second Following Distance Rule: count to 'one thousand four' after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object.

prompt: You are using the four-second rule in Wisconsin and it starts to snow. What should you do?
choices: Add a second for each adverse condition
Drop to two seconds so others don't cut in
explanation: Add a second for every adverse condition such as heavier traffic, rain, snow or ice.

prompt: In Wisconsin, what is the normal speed limit in a school zone when children are present?
explanation: The normal speed limit in a school zone when children are present is 15 mph.

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in Wisconsin residential areas?
explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential areas is 25 mph.

prompt: You leave downtown and enter an outlying district of a Wisconsin city where no speed limit is posted. What is the maximum speed there?
explanation: In outlying parts of Wisconsin cities and villages with no posted limit, the maximum is 35 mph. Elsewhere inside city or village limits the default is 25 mph.

prompt: On a Wisconsin highway where no other speed limit is set or posted, what is the speed limit?
explanation: In the absence of any other fixed or posted limit, Wisconsin's speed limit is 55 mph.

prompt: Unless signs show a different limit, what is the maximum speed Wisconsin law sets for freeways, including interstates?
explanation: Wisconsin's fixed limit is 70 mph on freeways, including interstates, and 65 mph on expressways, unless official signs show a different limit.

prompt: What is the speed limit in an alley in Wisconsin, unless a sign shows a different limit?
explanation: Wisconsin law sets a 15 mph limit in any alley unless official signs show a different limit.

prompt: The posted limit is 55 mph, but there is dense fog. Under Wisconsin law, what speed must you drive?
choices: At least 45 mph to avoid being rear-ended
No faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
explanation: No one may drive faster than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and hazards present, even if that is below the posted limit.

prompt: Can you be ticketed in Wisconsin for driving too slowly?
choices: Yes, if you drive so slowly that you impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic without a safety reason
explanation: Wisconsin law prohibits driving so slowly that you impede normal traffic unless reduced speed is needed for safety or to obey the law.

prompt: Under Wisconsin's sight distance rule, what must you do if you cannot see 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle?
choices: Slow down so you have better control
Switch on your high beams and keep your speed
Move closer to the vehicle ahead to follow its taillights
Speed up to get through the area quickly
explanation: Drivers need to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead. If you cannot, you must slow down so you keep control of the vehicle.

prompt: In Wisconsin, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
choices: After stopping, if it is safe and no sign prohibits it
Without stopping, if no one is coming
explanation: You can turn right on red if it is safe and no sign prohibits it. Stop first, yield to all traffic, then turn and stay in your lane.

prompt: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Wisconsin?
choices: From any street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping
explanation: You may turn left on red only when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding.

prompt: You are stopped at a red light on a two-way street and want to turn left onto a one-way street. May you turn on red in Wisconsin?
choices: No, left on red is only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
explanation: Wisconsin allows left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street; turning from a two-way street is not allowed.

prompt: How far before a turn at an intersection should you begin signaling in Wisconsin?
explanation: Start signaling about three seconds (about 100 feet) before the turn. If turning just after an intersection, start signaling once you cross it.

prompt: When may you cross a solid white line between lanes going the same direction in Wisconsin?
choices: Only if there is a hazard or you are turning within the next block
explanation: A solid white line between lanes means you cannot cross, unless there is a hazard or you are turning within the next block.

prompt: On a Wisconsin road divided by double solid yellow lines, when may you cross them to pass another vehicle?
choices: To pass a vehicle going less than half the speed limit when safe, unless it is farm equipment
To pass any vehicle going under the speed limit
explanation: The exceptions are turning into a driveway and passing a vehicle going less than half the speed limit when safe. Farm equipment is specifically excluded.

prompt: Which vehicles may NOT use a Wisconsin flex lane, even when it is open?
explanation: No large trucks can drive in the flex lane. Other vehicles may use it when the green arrow is shown.

prompt: When may you drive in a Wisconsin reserved lane (such as Buses Only) if you are not driving that type of vehicle?
choices: To turn across it within the next half block
explanation: It is illegal to travel in a reserved lane unless you need to turn across it within the next half of a block. If a bicyclist is in the lane, move behind them before turning.

prompt: At a metered freeway on-ramp in Wisconsin, where should you stop and when may you go?
choices: Go when the car ahead goes
Stop anywhere on the ramp and go when there is a gap
Pull completely up to the white stop line and go when your signal turns green
Stop at the end of the ramp and yield
explanation: Pull up to the white stop line so your tires trigger the pavement sensors; each lane has its own signal, and you may go when yours turns green. Disobeying the signal can bring a ticket.

prompt: In Wisconsin, a state highway route marker is a white sign with black numbers shaped like what?
choices: A milk jug with a spout at the bottom
explanation: Wisconsin's state road sign looks like a milk jug with a spout at the bottom. U.S. routes look like a badge, interstates use a red-and-blue shield, and county roads use a rounded rectangle.

prompt: A vehicle ahead of you displays this emblem. According to the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook, what speed could it be traveling?
explanation: The orange triangle with a reflective border is the slow moving vehicle emblem. It means the vehicle could travel at 25 mph or less, so slow down early.

prompt: What happens to traffic fines in a Wisconsin highway work zone marked with orange signs?
explanation: Traffic fines double in construction and maintenance work areas. Slow down and follow flaggers.

prompt: A pedestrian using a guide dog is crossing near your vehicle in Wisconsin. What must you do?
choices: Stop at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway
Honk so they know you are there
Stop only if they are in a marked crosswalk
explanation: Yield to pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane even if they are not in the intersection, stopping at least ten feet away until they are off the roadway.

prompt: You are already in a Wisconsin roundabout when an emergency vehicle with its siren on enters. What should you do?
choices: Exit at the next right, then pull over
explanation: If you are already in the roundabout, safely exit at the next right and then pull over. Avoid stopping in the roundabout.

prompt: When may you make a U-turn on a rural two-lane highway in Wisconsin?
choices: When it can be done safely without interfering with traffic and no sign prohibits it
explanation: You can make a U-turn on any rural two-lane highway if it is done safely and does not interfere with traffic, unless a sign prohibits it.

prompt: When may you use a paved shoulder to pass another vehicle on the right in Wisconsin?
choices: Only when the vehicle ahead is stopped or making a left turn
explanation: You can use a paved shoulder to go around someone only if they are stopped or making a left turn.

prompt: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Wisconsin (unless a sign shows a greater distance)?
explanation: Wisconsin law prohibits parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant unless a sign requires more distance.

prompt: In Wisconsin, how close to a crosswalk may you park?
explanation: You may not park closer than 15 feet to the near limits of a crosswalk, and you may never stop on a crosswalk.

prompt: In Wisconsin, you may not stop or park within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
explanation: Stopping or standing within 25 feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing is prohibited.

prompt: In Wisconsin, how far must you stay from a fire station's driveway entrance when stopping or parking?
explanation: You may not stop within 15 feet of a fire station driveway entrance or directly across the highway from it.

prompt: When parallel parking on the right side of a Wisconsin street, how close to the curb must your right wheels be?
explanation: Wisconsin law requires parallel-parked vehicles to have their wheels within 12 inches of the curb, facing the direction of traffic.

prompt: In Wisconsin, how close may you park to the entrance of a private driveway or alley?
explanation: Parking within 4 feet of the entrance to an alley, private road or driveway is prohibited.

prompt: When parallel parking in Wisconsin, how much space must you leave between your vehicle and the vehicles in front and behind?
explanation: A parallel-parked vehicle must be at least 2 feet from the vehicle in front and the vehicle behind, unless signs or markings show otherwise.

prompt: Under Wisconsin law, which of these is a place where you may never stop or leave your vehicle standing, even briefly?
choices: In a marked parking space on a one-way street
explanation: Stopping or standing within an intersection or on a crosswalk is prohibited at all times. Wisconsin's parking limits are 15 feet from a crosswalk and 25 feet from the nearest rail.

prompt: How far from a stopped school bus with flashing red lights must you stop in Wisconsin?
explanation: Stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights, whether it is on your side or the opposite side of the road.

prompt: You are driving on a divided highway with a barrier between directions. A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on the other side. What must you do in Wisconsin?
choices: You do not need to stop
explanation: On a divided highway, traffic on the opposite side from the bus does not need to stop.

prompt: You are stopped behind a Wisconsin school bus with flashing red lights. When may you go?
choices: When the children are off the bus
When the stop arm is half closed
When the red lights stop flashing
explanation: You can proceed once the red lights on the school bus have stopped flashing. Watch for children.

prompt: How much room must you give a bicyclist when passing in Wisconsin?
explanation: Give bicyclists at least three feet of room when you pass, and wait for oncoming traffic to clear first.

prompt: According to the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook, which statement about bicyclists in your traffic lane is true?
choices: Bicyclists can use the whole lane, so do not share the lane with them
You may squeeze past a bicyclist in the same lane if you leave one foot
Bicyclists must always ride on the shoulder
Bicyclists must pull off the road to let cars pass
explanation: Bicyclists can use the whole traffic lane, and drivers should not share a lane with them because they can move into your path without warning. Wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with at least three feet of room.

prompt: When an emergency vehicle is responding to a call in Wisconsin, how close may you follow it?
explanation: Drivers not on official business may not follow a responding emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet.

prompt: A fire truck has stopped at a fire in Wisconsin. How close to the driveway or road where it stopped may you park?
choices: No closer than 300 feet (and not within the same block)
Anywhere outside the fire hose area
explanation: You may not drive into or park within the block, or within 300 feet of the driveway or road, where fire apparatus has stopped for an alarm.

prompt: You hear a siren and see flashing lights coming from behind in Wisconsin. What should you do?
choices: Pull over to the side of the road and stop until it passes, but not in the middle of an intersection
Keep driving at the same speed
explanation: Pull over to the side and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. Do not stop in the middle of an intersection.

prompt: On a four-lane highway, you approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing. What does Wisconsin's Move Over law require?
choices: Use the shoulder to go around
Move into a lane not next to the stopped vehicle if safe; otherwise slow down
explanation: Move into a lane not nearest the stopped vehicle and stay there until past it. If you can't change lanes safely, slow down.

prompt: A car is stopped on the shoulder within a few feet of the road with its hazard lights on. Does Wisconsin's Move Over law apply?
choices: Only if a tow truck is present
No, it applies only to police cars
Yes, disabled vehicles with hazard lights are covered
explanation: Wisconsin's Move Over law covers disabled vehicles parked on or within 12 feet of the roadway, as well as emergency and roadside service vehicles.

prompt: A snowplow with flashing lights is clearing a 55 mph highway in Wisconsin. How far behind it should you stay?
explanation: Give snowplows at least 200 feet of room when their lights are flashing red, amber or green.

prompt: On a Wisconsin street with a posted speed limit of 30 mph, how close may you follow a snowplow that is plowing with its lights flashing?
explanation: Wisconsin law sets 200 feet on highways posted over 35 mph and 75 feet where the posted limit is 35 mph or less.

prompt: About how far behind and in front of a large truck are its No-Zones, according to the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook?
choices: 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front
100 feet behind and 50 feet in front
50 feet behind and 5 feet in front
500 feet behind and 100 feet in front
explanation: No-Zones are about 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front of large trucks. Speed up or drop back so the driver can see you.

prompt: You come upon livestock on a rural Wisconsin road. What should you do?
choices: Yield the right-of-way, slow down and keep a safe distance without honking
explanation: Yield the right-of-way to livestock on or along the highway. Do not honk, because it might scare the animals.

prompt: When must you use your headlights in Wisconsin?
choices: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and when you can't see 500 feet ahead
explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see a vehicle or person 500 feet (about one block) away and from a half hour past sunset to a half hour before sunrise.

prompt: In Wisconsin, when must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle?
explanation: Wisconsin law requires dimming your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.

prompt: You are following another vehicle at night in Wisconsin. Within what distance must you switch to low beams?
explanation: Wisconsin uses 500 feet both for oncoming vehicles and when following or approaching another vehicle from the rear. Many states use 200 or 300 feet here.

prompt: You hit a deer on a Wisconsin road. Which statement matches the Motorists' Handbook?
choices: You may keep the deer, and you should call police so they can issue a tag
You must pay a fine to the DNR
You must drag it into the ditch and leave
It is illegal to keep the deer
explanation: If you hit a deer you can keep it; if you don't want it, the next motorist can. Call police so they can issue a tag or know where the deer is.

prompt: In Wisconsin, a crash with no injuries must be reported to police if property damage reaches what amount?
explanation: Report a crash to police if there is an injury or death, or property damage of $1,000 or more.

prompt: You knock down a road sign and guard rail in a Wisconsin crash. At what amount of government property damage must you report it to police?
explanation: Damage to government property (such as signs or guard rails) of $200 or more must be reported to police.

prompt: Which Wisconsin motorcycle riders must wear an approved helmet?
choices: Operators and passengers under 18, and anyone riding with a motorcycle instruction permit
explanation: Helmets are required for operators and passengers under 18 and for anyone operating with a motorcycle instruction permit. Wisconsin has no helmet law for licensed riders 18 and older.

prompt: A 30-year-old is practicing with a Wisconsin motorcycle instruction permit. Must they wear a helmet?
choices: No, helmets are only for riders under 18
Yes, permit holders must wear an approved helmet with the chin strap fastened
explanation: Anyone riding with a cycle instruction permit, at any age, must wear an approved helmet with the chin strap fastened, plus eye protection.

prompt: A licensed 25-year-old Wisconsin rider wants to carry a 16-year-old passenger. What is required?
choices: The passenger must wear protective headgear
The passenger must hold a permit
explanation: No one may operate a motorcycle while carrying a passenger under 18 unless the passenger wears protective headgear.

prompt: When is eye protection NOT required for a Wisconsin motorcycle operator?
choices: When the motorcycle has a windshield rising at least 15 inches above the handlebars
explanation: All operators must wear eye protection unless the motorcycle has a windshield that rises at least 15 inches above the handlebars.

prompt: What rule applies to motorcycle eye protection worn during hours of darkness in Wisconsin?
choices: It is not required at night
It must be tinted to reduce glare
It may not be tinted or darkened
explanation: Eye protection worn during hours of darkness may not be tinted or darkened; only prescription photosensitive corrective lenses are an exception.

prompt: Is lane splitting (riding between lanes or in part of a lane occupied by another vehicle) legal in Wisconsin?
choices: No; the only exception is two motorcyclists who agree to ride side by side in one lane
explanation: Motorcyclists are entitled to a full lane and may not ride in any part of a lane occupied by another vehicle, except two cyclists who agree to ride side by side.

prompt: Your motorcycle is stopped at a red light that is not changing because no vehicle sensor detects you, and no other vehicles are present. Under Wisconsin law, what may you do?
choices: Turn around and find another route only
After stopping at least 45 seconds, proceed cautiously, yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians
Wait as long as it takes for the light to change
explanation: A motorcycle, moped or bicycle may proceed through a vehicle-actuated red signal after stopping at least 45 seconds if no other vehicles are present, yielding to all traffic. This does not apply to timed signals.

prompt: When must a motorcycle's headlight be on in Wisconsin?
choices: At all times when riding on a highway
explanation: When riding on a highway, the headlight and taillight must be on at all times.

prompt: How long is a Wisconsin motorcycle (Class M) instruction permit valid?
explanation: A Cycle Instruction Permit (CYCI) is valid for 6 months; after three permits you must complete or enroll in a basic rider course before getting a fourth.

prompt: A Wisconsin motorcycle permit holder wants to ride after dark. What is required?
choices: Nothing; permit holders may ride any time
They must be accompanied by a Class M license holder at least 25 years old with at least two years of licensed experience
Night riding is allowed only on freeways
They must carry a licensed passenger under 21
explanation: During hours of darkness a permit holder must be accompanied by a licensed person at least 25, with two years of licensed experience and a Class M license; that person may ride nearby rather than as a passenger.

prompt: Unless signs show otherwise, what is the speed limit on a street inside a Wisconsin city or village (not in an outlying district)?
explanation: Wisconsin law sets 25 mph on any highway within the limits of a city or village, other than outlying districts (35 mph), unless signs show a different limit.

prompt: A Wisconsin railroad crossing has a stop sign but no marked stop line. Where must you stop?
choices: At least 5 feet from the nearest rail
Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
At least 100 feet from the nearest rail
Right at the edge of the first rail
explanation: At a railroad crossing stop sign, stop at the marked stop line. If there is no stop line, stop not less than 15 nor more than 50 feet from the nearest rail.

prompt: How can a Wisconsin driver reduce their demerit point total?
choices: Attend an approved traffic safety course to remove 3 points, once in a three-year period
Pay a fee to remove all points
Take an online course to remove 5 points each year
Points cannot be reduced in any way
explanation: Attending an approved traffic safety course reduces your point total by three points. Only one reduction is allowed in a three-year period, and the courses are in person, not online.

prompt: You are passing a slow car on a two-lane Wisconsin highway posted at 55 mph. How fast may you legally go to finish the pass?
choices: Up to 65 mph, since passing allows 10 mph over the limit
Any speed needed, as long as you slow to 55 right after
No faster than 55 mph; the limit still applies when passing
Up to 60 mph, because short bursts over the limit are allowed
explanation: In Wisconsin it is illegal to drive faster than the posted speed limit, and you cannot go over the limit to pass another vehicle. If you cannot pass safely at or below the limit, stay behind.

prompt: To keep good control of your vehicle, how far ahead does the Wisconsin Motorists' Handbook say you need to be able to see?
